newsitem.title: GREECE: PRESS DIGEST - GREEK FINANCIAL NEWS- OCT 31.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - GREEK FINANCIAL NEWS- OCT 31.

text.p: Leading stories in the Greek financial press:
KATHIMERINI

--Balance of current accounts in first half 1996 worsens dramatically to 3.155 billion dollars, one of the highest figures in the last decade, up from 2,141 billion in first half 1995. The development is attributed to a great degree to the high cost of production, the 'hard drachma', as well as increased imports, decreased tourist exchange and to low absorption rates for European Union funds.

--Yesterday's meeting at the finance and national economy ministry puts final touches to bill to abolish tax breaks for specific professional groups and high income earners. the taxation of state titles is almost certain.
--National Economy and Finance Minister Yannos Papandoniou displeased with the lack of progress in the Athens Stock Exchange to deal with current problems.

--Piraeus Port Authority decides to raise tariffs for port services by 13 percent, effective 1997. Shipowners are expected to react negatively to the move, as many say that the increases are not in line with the level of services at the port.
--Joint defence, development and economy ministerial meeting looks at possibilities for expanding the armed force's construction programme at the Skaramangas and Elefsina shipyards.
IMERISIA

--The government is taking criticism of the operation of the bourse by banking and broker circles seriously and wants to strengthen the capital market by more controls, the expansion of the institutional framework and coordination of bourse authorities.

--Talk of forthcoming taxation of state titles and derivatives is expected to spur demand for today's treasury bill issue. However, yesterday's 0.40 percent increase in short-term interest rates created pressure on long-term rates and hindered the expression of interest from foreign investors.
--Firms obliged to readjust the value of their fixed assets by the end of the year will be those asked to pay higher taxes.
--The government will issue a 'housing bond' in mid-1997 to fund its two-year low-interest housing loans programme.

--Tax relief on housing loan interest will be untouched while the discount on life insurance poicies will be no higher than 15 percent on amounts up to 200,000 drachmas, Papandoniou is expected to recommend to Prime Minister Costas Simitis today.
KERDOS
--The finance ministry is ready to proceed with legislation to restrict the transfer of public servants from one area to the other, in an effort to plug gaps appearing in certain sectors.

Study shows that government services may have the required number of personnel but that many are being paid to work elsewhere. Some 6,000-8,000 teachers on the education ministry payroll are working in various government services that have nothing to do with education.
--Foreign investors reconsider their stance. The finance ministry's decision to issue a five-year bond with fixed interest has not taken into account the discouraging messages over the last few days.
--Union of Greek Banks and the finance ministry seek a mutually acceptable solution to the taxation of derivatives.
EXPRESS

--Papandoniou will present the finalised package of fiscal measures for the 1997 budget to Simitis today but taxation issues are still unresolved. Decision on whether the real estate tax will be a special charge or a permanent feature of the tax system has still not been taken.
--The readjustment of the values of business premises will be based on the year of their construction.
NAFTEMBORIKI
--Four economic policy measures decided by the government but many still pending. Wider social repurcussions appears to be a brake on the government taking the right decisions.
--Wave of strikes expected in November as the budget, tax issues, incomes policy, trading hours and education issues push workers into new protests.
--National Bank expects capital gain of 11 billion drachmas from the sealing of the contract with AGET and CALNAT.
--Maria Petrakis, Athens Newsroom +301 3311812-4
